native.inputBody: Hermes is waiting for your response.

connections.title: Registered gateways
connections.intro: Manage this device and every Hermes gateway it can reach through remote, SSH, or Cloud connections.
connections.stagedNote: Switch gateways from Sessions. Profiles, chats, messaging, and cron jobs stay with their gateway; work on other gateways keeps running.
connections.launchModeTitle: At startup, return to Sessions on the last-used gateway
connections.launchModeDesc: When off, Sessions opens on the Primary gateway.
connections.removeConfirmDesc: “{label}” will be removed from this app. The instance itself is not touched — you can add it again any time.
connections.kindLocalDesc: The Hermes runtime managed by this app.
connections.kindRemoteDesc: A Hermes gateway reachable over HTTP(S) — LAN, Tailscale, or the internet.
connections.kindCloudDesc: A hosted instance discovered through your Hermes Cloud account.
connections.kindSshDesc: A Hermes install reached over SSH.
connections.labelDesc: Required. Shown everywhere this instance appears; must be unique (e.g. “Homelab”, “Work laptop”).
connections.headersDesc: Sent with every HTTP and WebSocket request to this gateway — for access proxies such as Cloudflare Access (CF-Access-Client-Id / CF-Access-Client-Secret). Values are stored encrypted. Headers Hermes manages (Authorization, Cookie, Host…) are ignored.
connections.duplicateLocal: This app already manages a local connection — there can only be one.
connections.duplicateUrl: A connection to this gateway URL already exists (“{label}”).
connections.duplicateSsh: A connection to this SSH host already exists (“{label}”).
connections.localAddHint: Local is unavailable: the managed local connection already exists (there is only ever one).
connections.cloudAddHint: Tip: signing in under Hermes Cloud above discovers your agents automatically — use this form only to register a known instance URL by hand.

gateway.unavailableDesc: Connection settings can only be changed from the Hermes Desktop app on the computer running it.
gateway.title: Gateway Connection
gateway.intro: Local by default. Use remote when this app should drive a Hermes backend elsewhere. Gateway connections are machine-level; profiles are discovered from the gateways you connect.
gateway.envOverrideTitle: This connection was fixed by the way Hermes was launched.
gateway.envOverrideDesc: A startup setting outside the app chose this connection, so the options below are read-only. Restart Hermes without that setting — or ask whoever set it up — to change it here.
gateway.localDesc: Start a private Hermes backend on localhost. This is the default and works offline.
gateway.remoteDesc: Connect this desktop shell to a remote Hermes backend.
gateway.remoteAuthHint: Hosted gateways use OAuth or a username and password; self-hosted ones may use a session token.
gateway.cloudDesc: Sign in once to Hermes Cloud and pick from the agents on your account — no URL to paste.
gateway.cloudNeedsSignIn: Sign in to Hermes Cloud to discover the agents on your account.
gateway.cloudSignedInDesc: You are signed in. Pick an agent below; the session refreshes automatically.

cloudNoAgents.before: No agents found on this account. Create one in the

gateway.cloudSavedDesc: Use a saved gateway without changing your default. Sign in below to add instances. Manage names and sign-in in the saved connections list.
gateway.cloudDiscoverFailed: Could not load your Hermes Cloud agents
gateway.cloudConnectFailed: Could not connect to that agent
gateway.remoteUrlDesc: Base URL for the remote dashboard backend. Path prefixes are supported, for example /hermes.
gateway.probeError: Hermes can't reach that address. Check the URL and that the other computer is running Hermes — sign-in options appear once it answers.
gateway.authSignedInPassword: This gateway uses a username and password. You are signed in; the session refreshes automatically.
gateway.authSignedInOauth: This gateway uses OAuth. You are signed in; the session refreshes automatically.
gateway.authNeedsPassword: This gateway uses a username and password. Sign in to authorize this desktop app.
gateway.authNeedsOauth: This gateway uses OAuth. Sign in with {provider} to authorize this desktop app.
gateway.tokenDesc: The dashboard session token used for REST and WebSocket access. Leave blank to keep the saved token.
gateway.plainTextConfirmTitle: Store the gateway token in plain text?
gateway.plainTextConfirmDesc: No OS keyring service was found on this machine, so the token would be saved unencrypted in the app’s connection settings file, readable by any process running as this user. Install or enable your system keychain (GNOME Keyring or KWallet on Linux) for encrypted storage.
gateway.plainTextStoredDesc: Secure storage is unavailable, so the saved token is stored unencrypted in the app’s connection settings file on this machine. Install or enable your system keychain (GNOME Keyring or KWallet on Linux) to encrypt it.
gateway.keychainEncryptionTitle: Encrypt saved secrets with the OS keychain
gateway.keychainEncryptionDesc: Off by default. When on, gateway tokens and sign-in credentials are encrypted with your system keychain (Keychain Access, GNOME Keyring, or Windows DPAPI) — your system may ask for permission or a password. When off, they are stored as plain files readable only by your user account.
gateway.diagnosticsDesc: Reveal desktop.log in your file manager — useful when the gateway fails to start.
gateway.incompleteSignIn: Enter a remote URL and sign in before switching to remote.
gateway.incompleteToken: Enter a remote URL and session token before switching to remote.
gateway.incompleteSignInTest: Enter a remote URL and sign in before testing.
gateway.incompleteTokenTest: Enter a remote URL and session token before testing.
gateway.restartingMessage: Hermes Desktop will reconnect using the saved settings — the shell stays open.
gateway.sshDesc: Hermes is launched on the remote over SSH and tunneled to this app — nothing to start or expose yourself. Requires working key-based SSH access to the host.
gateway.sshTrustHint: The first presented host key is trusted and pinned; later changes fail closed.
gateway.sshHostDesc: user@host, or a Host alias from ~/.ssh/config.
gateway.sshHostPickDesc: A Host alias from ~/.ssh/config, or Custom to type one.
gateway.sshKeyDesc: Private key path. Blank = ssh-agent or ~/.ssh/config.
gateway.sshHermesPathDesc: Full path to the remote hermes binary. Blank = auto-detect.
gateway.sshButtonsHint: Save applies on the next launch. Connect reconnects now.
gateway.sshIncompleteHost: Enter an SSH host before connecting.
gateway.sshErrUnreachable: Could not reach that host over SSH. Check the host, port, and your network.
gateway.sshErrAuth: SSH authentication failed. Load your key into the ssh-agent (ssh-add) or set an IdentityFile in ~/.ssh/config — Hermes runs ssh non-interactively.
gateway.sshErrHostKey: The host key has CHANGED since you last connected. Verify this is expected, then run ssh-keygen -R <host> and reconnect.
gateway.sshErrNotInstalled: Hermes is not installed on the remote host. Install it there (curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | sh) or set the Hermes path.
gateway.sshErrPlatform: Unsupported remote platform. Hermes Desktop SSH mode supports Linux, macOS, and Windows remote hosts.
gateway.sshErrTimeout: SSH connection timed out. The host may be unreachable or asleep.
gateway.sshErrUpdateRequired: Update Hermes on the remote host before connecting with Desktop SSH.
gateway.sshErrInteractiveAuth: Tailscale SSH requires an interactive browser check. In Terminal, run `ssh <host> true`, complete the check, then retry — Hermes runs SSH non-interactively.

row.continuationOrigin: Automatic continuation — this conversation was compressed and continued
row.deleteDesc: This will permanently delete “{title}”. This cannot be undone.
